cases.title: AI tools that fit the editor
cases.subtitle: Godot Vibe Plugin · Google Summer of Code 2026
cases.role: GSoC contributor · editor plugin and backend
cases.summary: Built an editor workflow for prompt-driven asset generation, image editing, and scene automation during Google Summer of Code with the Python Software Foundation and pocketpy.

sections.title: The problem
sections.text: Generating an asset is only one part of a useful AI tool. The result also needs to fit an existing editor workflow, and the model's output needs a clear boundary before it changes a project.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: I built a GDScript editor plugin backed by FastAPI. For scene planning, I used a validated plan schema: the model returns structured data, and application code decides how to apply it. A deterministic rule-based fallback handles model unavailability.

sections.title: The decision
sections.text: I put provider-specific behavior behind a shared interface for PixelLab and GPT Image, then separated art-style content from the generation code. A five-stage pipeline uses JSON style packs so extending a style does not require changing the implementation.

sections.title: Where it landed
sections.text: The delivered workflow connects asset generation, editing, and scene automation inside Godot, with reusable style definitions and regression coverage for the generation pipeline.

sections.title: What I took forward
sections.text: My focus was making an AI capability usable as a developer tool: constrain what the model can request, keep provider differences contained, and make recurring content changes data-driven.

cases.title: Small changes inside a Python interpreter
cases.subtitle: Merged contributions to pocketpy
cases.summary: Contributed upstream fixes and standard-library compatibility features to pocketpy, with merged pull requests that make the work directly reviewable.

sections.title: The problem
sections.text: An embedded interpreter needs predictable behavior at small API boundaries. Missing standard-library helpers and numeric serialization differences can surface as application-level incompatibilities.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: In PR #487, I added operator.itemgetter and typing placeholders for ReadOnly and Required, then regenerated the embedded bindings through prebuild.py. The change was merged on March 26, 2026.

sections.title: The decision
sections.text: A later contribution focused on JSON integer and floating-point serialization. PR #519 records the implementation and subsequent round-trip refinements, and was merged on June 18, 2026.

sections.title: Where it landed
sections.text: Both contributions were accepted into the upstream project. The linked pull requests show the implementation, discussion, and merge history.

sections.title: What I took forward
sections.text: This work connects application-level Python behavior to the internals of an embedded runtime, including generated bindings and numeric representation.

cases.title: Debugging the boundary between contact and motion
cases.subtitle: SpellTide / sbx_extension · Godot native systems
cases.summary: Contributed to the C++ physics layer of a wrap-around tile world, focusing on cube-body contacts, collision debugging, and the boundary between simulation state and rendering.

sections.title: The problem
sections.text: A small visible symptom—an object shaking against a wall—can come from several different layers: contact detection, penetration correction, the collision normal, or how the controller applies motion.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: I investigated the behavior by narrowing flat-wall and rounded-corner cases, examining contact creation/removal events, and tracing separation and position values. This made it possible to distinguish a contact repeatedly disappearing from a contact that remained active but resolved unstably.

sections.title: The decision
sections.text: The useful design boundary was between character control and physical motion. A controller that resets velocity every frame has different requirements from a body that preserves momentum. I also learned to evaluate rendering optimizations against whether geometry is shared and how often state changes.

sections.title: Where it landed
sections.text: The work sits within a native extension that exposes cube-body physics, chunked broad-phase queries, collision callbacks, and torus tilemap support to Godot and PocketPy.

sections.title: What I took forward
sections.text: The fastest route through a difficult systems bug was to choose a discriminating observation, collect it at the right layer, and revise the hypothesis when the evidence changed.

cases.title: Reliable integrations across tenant boundaries
cases.subtitle: K.C. Voicebotics · Full-stack and platform integrations
cases.summary: Built backend integration workflows for a conversational voice-AI product, with tenant-aware authentication and failure handling exposed through a React operator console.

sections.title: The problem
sections.text: A third-party integration becomes an operational concern when multiple tenants have different credentials and a provider can fail, retry, or deliver the same event more than once.

sections.title: My contribution
sections.text: I engineered an OAuth 2.0 pipeline with dynamic redirect URIs and per-tenant token refresh. Integration onboarding moved toward configuration entries, reducing repeated implementation work for new connections.

sections.title: The decision
sections.text: I used idempotent webhook handlers and exponential-backoff retries to keep external state consistent under failure. On the request path, I restructured Spring Boot routing and batched downstream API calls, with a React console supporting preview and approval workflows.

sections.title: Where it landed
sections.text: The work connects tenant authentication, asynchronous requests, and retry behavior into an operator-facing workflow, with configuration-based onboarding and explicit handling for repeated or failed provider events.

sections.title: What I took forward
sections.text: The integration boundary needs explicit behavior for repeat delivery, stale credentials, and partial failure—not just a successful first request.
